sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Make a website that, if everyone saw and used it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- To look at the page yourself, serve it locally and screenshot it in headless Chrome (Chrome is
  installed, and a driver such as puppeteer-core or playwright can be npm-installed here). Save every
  screenshot you look at as a .jpg file, never .png: each image you read stays in your context, and a
  long session of large .png files can hit the provider's per-request image limit and end the run.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

  • 4. Depth: 5–6 cm (2–2.4 in). Let chest recoil completely. Never pause >10s.
02 / CHOKING, STROKE & BLEED IMMEDIATE
  • • Choking: Alternate 5 back blows (between shoulder blades) + 5 abdominal thrusts (fist thumb-in just above navel).
  • • Stroke (B.E.F.A.S.T.): Balance, Eyes, Face droop, Arm drift, Speech slur, Time (write down exact minute!). No aspirin.
  • • Severe Bleed: Continuous firm direct pressure for 3–5 full min (do not peek). Limb artery → Tourniquet 5–8 cm above wound.
03 / NERVOUS SYSTEM RESET 60–90 SEC
  • • Physiological Sigh (×3): Deep nasal inhale (80%) + sharp top-up nasal inhale (100%) → long, slow mouth exhale.
  • • 90-Second Chemical Rule: Bloodstream adrenaline clears in 90s if you don’t feed the mental story. Never send a message inside the 90s wave.
  • • H.A.L.T. Check: Am I Hungry, Angry, Lonely, or Tired?
04 / CONFLICT & NOISY TRUST 5 MIN
  • • Drop "Always / Never" generalizations and counter-blame.
  • • Repair Script: "When [neutral observation], I feel [emotion] because I need [shared value]. Would you be willing to [concrete action]?"
  • • Generous Tit-for-Tat: In a noisy world, forgive isolated misunderstandings once, communicate clearly, and maintain firm boundaries.
05 / WHO ORS & SAFE WATER HOUSEHOLD
  • • WHO Oral Rehydration Solution: Mix 1 Liter clean water + 6 level tsp sugar (25g) + ½ level tsp salt (2.6g).
  • • Taste Check: Must taste no saltier than tears (excess salt pulls water out of the body).
  • • Water Disinfection: 2 drops plain 6% bleach per 1L (4 drops if cloudy), wait 30 min; or 1 min rolling boil (3 min >2,000m).
06 / THE 100× GOOD MULTIPLIER LIFETIME
  • • Reject Fatalism: Child survival rose from 57% (1800) to 96.3% today; extreme poverty fell from 38% (1990) to 8.5%.
  • • 100× Rule: Top-tested health programs protect a child from malaria for ~$5.50 and save a statistical life for ~$4,000.
  • • Zero-Cost Multipliers: Donate blood 3×/yr & join the stem cell registry.
⚡ IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY ACTION CHECKLIST

First 60 Seconds in a Medical or Household Crisis

1

Unresponsive / Not Breathing Normally

Call 911 / 112 / 999 on speakerphone. Push hard & fast at center of chest: 100–120 BPM, 5–6 cm deep. Send someone for an AED. Ignore occasional gasps.

2

Severe Choking (Cannot Speak/Cough)

Bend person forward: give 5 sharp back blows between shoulder blades with heel of hand, then 5 abdominal thrusts (fist thumb-in just above navel). Repeat.

3

Suspected Stroke (B.E.F.A.S.T.)

Check Balance, Eyes, Face droop, Arm drift (10s), Speech slur. Call emergency services immediately and record the exact Last Known Well minute. Give NO food, drink, or aspirin.

4

Life-Threatening Bleeding

Press clean cloth directly on wound with both hands—hold firm, uninterrupted pressure for 3–5 full minutes (do NOT lift cloth to peek). For arterial limb bleed, apply tourniquet high & tight.

5

Dehydration / Oral Rehydration (ORS)

Dissolve 6 level teaspoons sugar + ½ level teaspoon salt in 1 Liter of clean/boiled water. Taste before giving: must be no saltier than tears. Sip continuously.

6

Acute Panic Attack / Shock

Have person sit upright. Guide 3 Physiological Sighs: deep inhale through nose + second sharp top-up inhale through nose → long slow exhale through pursed lips.

Sources: AHA/ERC Resuscitation Guidelines · WHO ORS Standards · Stanford Neurobiology · Axelrod Cooperation Tournaments · Our World in Data / GiveWell.

# The Human Field Manual

An offline-ready, interactive citizen training and calibration website designed so that if everyone saw and practiced it, it would save lives, disarm conflict, and multiply human good across five concentric scales of agency:

1. **Scale I — The Body (First 4 Minutes):** Interactive 110 BPM Hands-Only CPR Rhythm & Cerebral Perfusion Simulator (with procedural Web Audio metronome and spacebar/touch compression trainer) + emergency triage protocols for Choking (5+5), Stroke (B.E.F.A.S.T.), and Severe Bleeding.
2. **Scale II — The Nervous System (First 60 Seconds):** Live Alveolar & Vagus Nerve Breath Pacer modeling Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia (Physiological Sigh, Box Breathing, 4-7-8 Downshift) + Dr. Jill Bolte Taylor's 90-Second Adrenaline Clearance Timer and Cognitive Distortion Defusion tool.
3. **Scale III — The Conversation (5 Minutes):** Branching Nonviolent Conflict De-escalation Simulator + Interactive Game-Theory Sandbox modeling Robert Axelrod & Martin Nowak's *Generous Tit-for-Tat* under communication noise.
4. **Scale IV — The Household (First 24 Hours):** Interactive WHO Oral Rehydration Solution (SGLT1 Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter) Lab demonstrating the exact `6 tsp sugar : 1/2 tsp salt per 1L` hypotonic ratio + Emergency Safe Water Disinfection Calculator.
5. **Scale V — The World (Lifetime Leverage):** Empirical Reality Calibrator (curing fatalism with historical poverty and child survival data) + The 100× Life-Saving Leverage & Biological Donor Calculator.
6. **Pocket Field Card:** Printable and downloadable high-resolution 1-page emergency & high-leverage reference card.

## Architecture
- Entry point: `index.html` + `main.js` + `styles.css`
- Modules: `src/audio.js`, `src/section1-cpr.js`, `src/section2-breath.js`, `src/section3-conflict.js`, `src/section4-water.js`, `src/section5-leverage.js`, `src/section6-card.js`
- 100% self-contained: zero network requests, zero external assets, and zero `localStorage`/cookie dependencies for full sandboxed offline compatibility.

I have built **The Human Field Manual** (`index.html`, `main.js`, `styles.css`, and modular ES modules in `src/`), a self-contained, offline-ready interactive training and calibration website designed to give every person the five highest-leverage practical skills for saving lives, preventing harm, and multiplying human good:

### What Was Built

1. **Scale I — The Body (First 4 Minutes: Save a Life in Front of You)** (`src/section1-cpr.js`, `src/audio.js`)
   - **Interactive Hands-Only CPR Rhythm & Cerebral Perfusion Simulator:** A 60fps anatomical and hemodynamic canvas paired with a procedural Web Audio 110 BPM metronome. Users can practice compressions via `SPACEBAR` or touch/click to see how a 100–120 BPM cadence at 5–6 cm depth sustains cerebral perfusion pressure above the 60% survival threshold—and why pausing for more than 10 seconds collapses brain blood flow.
   - **Emergency Field Protocols:** Scannable step-by-step triage guides for **Cardiac Arrest (CPR & AED)**, **Choking (5 Back Blows + 5 Abdominal Thrusts)**, **Stroke (B.E.F.A.S.T. Symptom Check)**, and **Severe Bleeding (Direct Pressure & Tourniquet)**.

2. **Scale II — The Nervous System (First 60 Seconds: Steady an Overwhelmed Mind)** (`src/section2-breath.js`)
   - **Live Alveolar & Vagus Nerve Breath Pacer:** Visualizes lung alveolar recruitment and **Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia (RSA)** across three clinical protocols (**Physiological Sigh**, **Box Breathing**, and **4–7–8 Downshift**) with optional procedural harmonic audio cues.
   - **90-Second Adrenaline Clearance Timer & Cognitive Defusion Tool:** Implements Dr. Jill Bolte Taylor’s 90-second catecholamine clearance rule alongside an interactive reframing tool for the four universal cognitive distortions (*Mind-Reading, Catastrophizing, All-or-Nothing, and Emotional Reasoning*).

3. **Scale III — The Conversation (5 Minutes: Disarm Conflict & Survive Noise)** (`src/section3-conflict.js`)
   - **Interactive De-escalation Fork Simulator:** Walk through three high-friction scenarios (Partner/Home, Workplace Blame, Polarized Belief) and compare how counter-attacks or defensive minimizing affect **Mutual Threat (Cortisol)** vs. **Problem-Solving Bandwidth**, contrasted with high-leverage Nonviolent Communication / Steelmanning repair scripts.
   - **Game Theory of Noisy Trust Sandbox:** An interactive 28-round simulation based on Robert Axelrod and Martin Nowak’s research demonstrating why *Strict Tit-for-Tat* collapses into mutual vendettas as soon as misunderstanding noise exceeds 5%, and why *Generous Tit-for-Tat* (forgiving isolated noise while holding firm boundaries) is mathematically essential for human cooperation.

4. **Scale IV — The Household (First 24 Hours: Public Health Formulas)** (`src/section4-water.js`)
   - **WHO Oral Rehydration Solution (SGLT1 Cotransporter) Interactive Lab:** Allows users to mix sugar and salt in 1 Liter of water while watching a live cellular simulation of intestinal enterocytes, showing why **6 level teaspoons sugar + ½ level teaspoon salt** (~242 mOsm/L) unlocks SGLT1 sodium-glucose pumps, whereas soda or excess salt causes hyperosmolar water loss.
   - **Emergency Safe Water Disinfection Calculator:** Computes exact household bleach drop counts (5–6% vs. 8.25%), turbidity adjustments, rolling boil altitude rules, and Solar UV (SODIS) protocols.

5. **Scale V — The World (Lifetime: Cure Fatalism & Multiply Good by 100×)** (`src/section5-leverage.js`)
   - **Global Reality Calibrator:** Tests user intuition against empirical historical trajectories on extreme poverty, child survival (96.3%), and the heavy-tailed effectiveness distribution of global health programs.
   - **Personal 100× Leverage & Biological Donor Simulator:** Calculates concrete human outcomes (malaria nets, Vitamin A doses, statistical lives saved, and local patients supported via zero-cost blood donation, stem-cell registry, and teaching CPR/ORS).

6. **Section 06 — Folding Pocket Field Card & Quick SOS Modal** (`src/section6-card.js`)
   - Includes a zero-scroll **Quick SOS Emergency Modal**, print stylesheet (`@media print`), plain-text clipboard export, and a client-side canvas generator that exports a high-resolution **1-Page Folding Pocket Field Card (`.jpg`)** for offline use.
